# rishi


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

rishi lets you use a language model from Python with the same calls,
whether the model runs on your machine or on a remote server. Each way
of running a model is a backend. Four backends run models locally:
LiteRT-LM, llama.cpp, MLX and Ollama. Three backends send the
conversation to another program or server: a hosted API such as OpenAI
or Anthropic, your Claude Code installation, and GitHub Copilot. Each of
these seven has its own message format and its own way to pass images
and tool calls.

rishi uses one conversation format for all of them. The conversation is
called the history. The history is a Python list of message dicts in the
OpenAI format, such as `{'role': 'user', 'content': 'hi'}`. It is stored
in `chat.hist`. Every backend reads and writes that list. You can start
a conversation on a small local model, give the list to a hosted model,
and the hosted model continues the conversation.

The parts that all backends share come from
[Urai](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai), which is published on PyPI
as `uraiyadal`. These are the `Chat` class, tool calling, streaming,
options and recorded replies. rishi adds the seven backends and
registers them with Urai. `from rishi import *` gives you the names from
Urai and from rishi.

## Install

The base package includes LiteRT-LM and the three backends that send the
conversation to another program or server. The other local backends need
optional extras. Install only the extras you use:

``` sh
pip install rishi                # LiteRT-LM, hosted APIs, Claude Code and GitHub Copilot
pip install 'rishi[llama]'       # llama.cpp, for GGUF model files
pip install 'rishi[mlx]'         # MLX, on Apple Silicon Macs
pip install 'rishi[mlx-vlm]'     # MLX vision and audio models
pip install 'rishi[ollama]'      # Ollama; on Linux before Python 3.14 this also installs zstandard
pip install 'rishi[all]'         # every extra above
```

You can combine extras, as in `rishi[llama,mlx]`. rishi imports a
backend module only when a chat first needs it. A missing extra causes
no error until you ask for that backend. The hosted backends use their
usual credentials. Hosted APIs need an API key in the environment.
Claude Code needs a signed-in `claude` command. Copilot needs a GitHub
sign-in.

## Chat

`Chat(model)` opens one conversation. The model name selects the
backend. rishi recognizes a `.litertlm` build, a `-GGUF` repo, an
`mlx-community` repo, an Ollama `hf.co/` id, and a hosted name such as
`gpt-5.1`. A prefix such as `claude/` or `copilot/` selects the backend
directly. With no model, `Chat` uses LiteRT-LM and its default model,
Gemma 4 E2B. The [core](core.html) page lists the exact rules.

Call the chat with a prompt to send one turn. The call returns the
reply, a dict that Urai calls a `Resp`. Each call appends the prompt and
the reply to `chat.hist`. The second question below is therefore asked
with the first exchange in the history. `resp_text` returns the answer
text from a reply. `close()` frees the model memory.

``` python
chat = Chat(gemma4_e2b)
print(resp_text(chat('Give one fact about lobsters.')))
print(resp_text(chat('Give one more.')))
chat.close()
```

    Lobsters are crustaceans, which means they have a hard exoskeleton and eight legs.
    Lobsters are known for their ability to change their color and texture to blend in with their surroundings, a behavior called camouflage.

## Streaming

Pass `stream=True` to receive a reply as it is generated. The call then
returns an iterator of markdown strings instead of one reply. Urai
renders the events of every backend into the same markdown. Thinking and
tool calls look the same on every backend. Pass `stream='raw'` to
receive the chunk dicts that the markdown is built from.

``` python
chat = Chat(gemma4_e2b)
for markdown in chat('Write a two-line poem about rain.', stream=True):
    print(markdown, end='', flush=True)
chat.close()
```

    Soft drops tap on the pane,
    Washing the world clean again.

## Images

To ask about a picture, pass a list instead of a string. The list holds
the prompt text and the image. The image can be a `Path`, raw bytes or a
`PIL.Image`. Every backend that accepts images accepts the same list.
The model must accept image input. Gemma 4 on LiteRT-LM does. The page
of each backend names other models.

``` python
chat = Chat(gemma4_e2b)
image = repo_root()/'nbs/images.jpeg'
display(Image.open(image))
print(resp_text(chat(['Describe this image in one sentence.', image])))
chat.close()
```

![](index_files/figure-commonmark/cell-4-output-1.png)

    A medium-sized, reddish-brown German Shepherd is looking attentively off to the side with its mouth slightly open.

## Audio

Pass audio in the same list as the prompt, as a file path or as bytes.
The model needs an audio encoder. Gemma 4 on LiteRT-LM has one. Some
llama.cpp and MLX models have one. Claude Code, Ollama and text-only
models raise an error. They do not drop the clip.

``` python
chat = Chat(gemma4_e2b)
audio = repo_root()/'nbs/speech.wav'
print(resp_text(chat(['Transcribe this clip.', audio])))
chat.close()
```

    Dancing in the masquerade, idol truth in plain sight jaded, pop, roll, click, dot, who will I be today or not? But such a tide as moving seems asleep, too full for sound and foam, when that drew from out the boundless deep turns again home, twilight and evening bell and after that.

## One conversation across seven backends

Every backend uses the same history format. A conversation can move
between backends. The example below has seven legs. Each leg opens a new
`Chat` with `messages=history`, sends one prompt, and passes the longer
history to the next leg. The first leg uses Gemma on LiteRT-LM. Its
prompt gives the code word “amber”. The next six legs use Qwen3 on
Ollama, Qwen3 on MLX, Qwen3 on llama.cpp, GPT-4.1 through the hosted
API, Claude Haiku through Claude Code, and GPT-4.1 through Copilot. Each
of them is asked for the code word and answers “amber”. It can know this
only from the history.

The example downloads four local models. The last three legs need their
credentials.

``` python
legs = [
    ('LiteRT', gemma4_e2b, {}),
    ('Ollama', f'ollama/{ollama_qwen}', {'think': True}),
    ('MLX', mlx_qwen, {}),
    ('llama.cpp', llama_qwen, {'n_ctx': 4096}),
    ('cloud', 'gpt-4.1', {}),
    ('Claude', 'claude/haiku', {}),
    ('Copilot', 'copilot/gpt-4.1', {}),
]

history = []
for i, (name, model, options) in enumerate(legs):
    chat = Chat(model, messages=history, **options)
    prompt = (
        'The code word is amber. Start a travel log with one short sentence.'
        if i == 0 else
        f'What is the code word? Add one short sentence saying {name} received this conversation.'
    )
    reply = chat(prompt)
    print(f'{name}: {resp_text(reply)}')
    history = list(chat.hist)
    chat.close()

print([m['role'] for m in history])
```

    LiteRT: Amber awaits.
    Ollama: The code word is **amber**. Ollama received this conversation.

    Fetching 9 files:   0%|                                                                                                                 | 0/9 [00:00<?, ?it/s]
    Fetching 9 files: 100%|███████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████| 9/9 [00:00<00:00, 1912.59it/s]

    MLX: The code word is **amber**. MLX received this conversation.

    llama_context: n_ctx_seq (4096) < n_ctx_train (40960) -- the full capacity of the model will not be utilized

    llama.cpp: The code word is **amber**. llama.cpp received this conversation.
    cloud: The code word is amber. Cloud received this conversation.
    Claude: The code word is amber. Claude received this conversation.
    Copilot: The code word is amber. Copilot received this conversation.
